name: Reproduce whether a null patch removes unknown delegator top-level keys
details: dispatched: self — output landed in this ledger. On b35165ff, a copy of the revision-38 delegator file plus a non-empty handled_wakes list: {"handled_wakes":null} with delegator update --writer delegator --expect-revision 38 removes the key and keeps known fields; the list contents are discarded and the receipt removed list stays empty. A second null writes again and bumps revision. A non-null patch of that key is refused before read, with no revision and no command. Any update that leaves the non-empty key is blocked; recovery is only "rehome this duty or name it for removal". A watch-only update cannot rehome while the key remains. The same update can add watch rows and null the key, then migrate plans clean. View lists the unknown path and watch rows, with no nonterminal count, earliest at, or clear command. A stale expect-revision refuses with current_revision; detail is "file is at revision N". A non-delegator writer is refused. state check refuses the delegator schema as schema-unsupported. The live .kaola file stayed revision 38. Design: keep the null update as the named removal; put collection, id, revision, the executable command, and the same-update rehome prompt on the refusal and on view; a repeat null of an absent unknown key does not write; view computes the diagnosis and writes nothing. Do not change record-contract.
